summary.en: Use **must** and **have to** for obligation, **mustn't** for prohibition, and **don't have to** or **needn't** when something is not necessary. _You **mustn't** park here_ means it is forbidden; _You **don't have to** park here_ means you may choose.
summary.es: Aquí está la gran trampa: mustn't es «prohibido» y don't have to es «no hace falta». No son lo mismo. Must suele expresar una obligación que sale del hablante; have to, una norma o circunstancia externa.

form: **have to / has to** + infinitive; questions and negatives with _do_: _Do you have to…?_
**don't / doesn't have to** or **needn't** + infinitive: it is not necessary

uses.text: **Strong obligation from the speaker**: _I **must** call my mother tonight._
**Rules and external obligation**: _Employees **have to** wear a badge._ _I **had to** show my passport._
**Prohibition**: _You **mustn't** use your phone during the test._
**No obligation**: _You **don't have to** book; there are always free tables._ _You **needn't** wait for me._

note.en: Needn't is more common in British English and a little more formal.
note.es: Needn't es más británico y algo más formal.

uses.text: **Past and future**: _We **had to** queue for an hour._ _You'll **have to** pay a fine._

mistakes.wrong: You mustn't bring a lunch. There's a canteen.
mistakes.right: You don't have to bring a lunch. There's a canteen.

why.en: Mustn't means it is forbidden. For no need, use don't have to.
why.es: «No hace falta» es don't have to; mustn't significa «prohibido».

mistakes.right: Yesterday I had to work late.

why.en: Must has no past form. Use had to.
why.es: Must no tiene pasado: had to.

mistakes.wrong: Does she must wear a uniform?
mistakes.right: Does she have to wear a uniform?

why.en: Must is a modal and does not take do. Have to does.
why.es: Must no lleva do; have to sí.

mistakes.wrong: I have to not forget my keys.

why.en: Use mustn't for a strong warning to yourself or others.

examples.en: I must remember to renew my passport before the summer.
Drivers have to carry their licence at all times.
examples.es: Los conductores tienen que llevar el carnet siempre encima.

examples.en: You mustn't leave valuables in the car.
You don't have to wear a tie, but a smart shirt would be good.
examples.es: No hace falta que lleves corbata, pero una camisa elegante estaría bien.

examples.en: We needn't hurry; the film doesn't start until eight.
She had to leave the meeting early to collect her son.
Do you have to work at the weekend?
If the test is positive, you'll have to stay at home for five days.
Passengers must not walk across the railway lines.

practice.prompt: You ___ shout in the library. It's against the rules.
It's a free event, so you ___ buy a ticket.
When I was a student, I ___ get up at six for my part-time job.

explanation.en: Must has no past form, so use had to.

practice.prompt: ___ you have to wear a helmet on that building site?

explanation.en: Have to makes questions with do.
